identity.title: Rapid genotyping of FecB mutation in sheep using CRISPR-Cas12a orthology-assisted assay.

content.abstract: Accurate genotyping of the Fecundity Booroola (FecB) gene, a key determinant of ovine fecundity, is essential for effective breeding programs. However, current methods are largely constrained by their reliance on specialized equipment and high operational costs, which collectively limit their applicability for large-scale, on-site genetic screening. To address these challenges, we systematically evaluated five Cas12a orthologs and identified Gs12-19 as the optimal candidate. Based on this, we developed a novel detection platform integrating the CRISPR-Gs12-19 system with allele-specific amplification and fluorescence-based signal readout, which enables discrimination between homozygous wild-type sheep (AA) and FecB mutation carriers (AG or GG, collectively designated as RG). Coupled with a portable blue-light excitation device and a custom-designed Red Channel Quantification (RedQ) analytical program, the platform was field-tested on 153 randomly selected samples from a core crossbred sheep population. The method achieved 98% accuracy in mutation-carrier classification when benchmarked against Sanger sequencing. Collectively, this study offers a rapid, visually interpretable, and field-deployable platform for FecB mutation-carrier screening with high sensitivity and specificity, providing a practical solution to accelerate marker-assisted selection in sheep breeding.
